title: AI Learns the Hidden DNA Code That Marks Enhancers Across Species
key_facts: EnhancerDetector, a convolutional neural network by Solis, Sterling-Lentsch, Halfon and Girgis, published in BMC Genomics.
Predicts whether a DNA window is an enhancer (a DNA stretch that switches genes on or off) from sequence alone.
Outperformed existing methods in precision and F1 score on human, mouse and fly datasets.
Trained on human data, it transferred to mouse and fly; fine-tuning worked with as few as 20,000 enhancer sequences.
Class activation maps show which parts of the sequence drive each prediction.
Of six predicted candidates tested in transgenic flies, five drove reporter expression and four of those matched earlier literature.
Authors position it as a first-stage annotation tool for newly sequenced genomes.
quote_evidence: EnhancerDetector consistently outperformed existing methods in precision and F1 score.
Of six candidates tested, five drove reporter expression.
Moreover, four of the five exhibited expression patterns consistent with those reported in the earlier literature.
why_it_matters_hint: A sequence-only tool could help annotate new genomes without years of experiments.
event_date: Study in BMC Genomics; article dated 4 Oct 2026
notes: Article carries Scienmag's text (credited at the end); Scienmag named as source. Only six fly candidates were tested.
